questions.text:
Consider the following psuedocode:
x: integer := 1  
y: integer := 2   
procedure add  
    x:= x + y    
procedure second (P: Procedure)  
    x: integer := 2      
    p()   
procedure first  
    y: integer := 3
    second (add) 
first () 
write_integer(x)
What does it print if the language uses dynamic scoping with deep binding?
questions.solution: Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

x is the same variable p (by reference), c is copied. Each call does x = x + 1 before the recursion, and multiplies by x only after returning:

p goes 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 9, then c reaches 0 and returns 1. On the way back each of the 4 levels multiplies by x, which is now 9.

[latex]9^4=6561[/latex]

Answer: 6561
